story.title: UN Secretary-General Guterres Calls for AI Regulation and Peace in Final Address
story.summary: In his final address to the UN General Assembly, Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged world leaders to regulate artificial intelligence, end ongoing wars, and prioritize climate change. He emphasized the need for an overhaul of UN institutions to better address global challenges and called for a collaborative approach among superpowers. Guterres also condemned violence in Gaza and the expansion of settlements in the West Bank.

explore_lenses.label: Can the UN turn AI warnings into rules?
explore_lenses.title: The current AI track is a forum, not a treaty process
explore_lenses.summary: Guterres’s call builds on UN mechanisms created in 2025, but those mechanisms currently develop shared evidence and approaches rather than binding global AI rules.

claims.text: UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/79/325 created an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance; the Dialogue covers safety, capacity-building, interoperability, human rights, transparency, accountability and human oversight.
The UN says the Global Dialogue is not a negotiating forum and does not itself produce binding agreements; its output is a co-chairs’ summary intended to inform later governance decisions.
Guterres’s position is that national action alone is inadequate because AI risks cross borders, and that voluntary, unverifiable pauses cannot manage risks when they become too great.

explore_lenses.label: Why is UN reform central to his peace appeal?
explore_lenses.title: Veto power limits the UN’s ability to act on wars
explore_lenses.summary: Guterres links peace to institutional reform because the Security Council—the body with primary responsibility for international peace and security—can be blocked by its permanent members.

claims.text: The UN’s Security Council-reform process has continued through intergovernmental negotiations since 2008, covering representation, membership and related issues; the General Assembly is still carrying those negotiations forward.

CNA reported that seven draft Security Council resolutions were vetoed in 2024, the highest annual total since 1986; analyst Daniel Forti said this illustrates the limits of the institution when its major powers do not cooperate.

Germany has argued for a reform package that improves both representation and effectiveness, including an interim arrangement under which new permanent members would not exercise a veto until a review 15 years after reform. China, in the same UN negotiation, described the veto as a foundational part of the UN’s institutional design that should be addressed only as part of a package solution.

explore_lenses.label: What could follow Guterres’s final assembly?
explore_lenses.title: Diplomacy may continue, but Guterres leaves on December 31
explore_lenses.summary: The General Assembly week can create opportunities for leader-level contacts, while Guterres’s remaining leverage is chiefly convening and advocacy as the process to choose his successor is already underway.

claims.text: Guterres’s second term ends on December 31, 2026, and the General Assembly and Security Council presidents formally began the selection process for the next secretary-general in March 2026.

Guterres said High-Level Week can enable meetings among leaders facing confrontations and pointed to a 2025 meeting between the United States and several Muslim-majority countries that he said helped lead to a Gaza peace plan.

Forecast: Maya Ungar of Conflict Armament Research told CNA that discussions during the Assembly could lead to concrete action after the week, and assessed Iran as the issue most likely to see such movement.

Guterres’s immediate Gaza position is that the peace plan should be fully implemented with unrestricted humanitarian aid and that what he calls the creeping annexation of the West Bank must stop; he argues that a two-state solution is necessary for peace.

story_report.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres used his final address to the General Assembly to urge governments to regulate artificial intelligence, end wars, confront climate change and reform UN institutions. He also condemned violence in Gaza and the expansion of settlements in the West Bank. The speech set out priorities rather than creating new commitments or enforcement measures, leaving action on conflicts and institutional change to member states after the Assembly. Guterres’s second term ends on Dec. 31, 2026.

sections.heading: AI Governance Framework Takes Shape
sections.body: The UN has already created an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance. The Dialogue covers issues including safety, capacity-building, interoperability, human rights, transparency, accountability and human oversight, but it is not a negotiating forum and cannot itself produce binding agreements. Guterres has argued that national measures alone cannot manage cross-border AI risks and that voluntary, unverifiable pauses are insufficient once risks become too great.

sections.heading: Security Council Reform Divides Members
sections.body: Intergovernmental negotiations on Security Council reform have continued since 2008, focusing on representation, membership and related questions. CNA reported that seven Council resolutions were vetoed in 2024, the highest annual number since 1986; analyst Daniel Forti said the record illustrated the institution’s limits when major powers do not cooperate. Germany has proposed an interim arrangement limiting veto use by new permanent members, while China has said the veto must be considered only within a package solution.

sections.heading: Gaza Demands Frame UN Transition
sections.body: Guterres has called for full implementation of a Gaza peace plan, unrestricted humanitarian aid and an end to what he describes as the creeping annexation of the West Bank, arguing that a two-state solution is necessary for peace. He has also said the Assembly’s high-level week can bring together leaders in confrontation, citing a 2025 meeting that he said helped lead to a Gaza peace plan. The General Assembly and Security Council presidents formally began the process to select his successor in March 2026.

Security Council reform has no agreed text or timetable, and changing its core structure would require unusually broad agreement among member states.

related_stories.summary: Presley Gerber, the 27-year-old son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and entrepreneur Rande Gerber, has died. Gerber was found unresponsive at a rehabilitation facility in Los Angeles shortly after checking in.

related_stories.title: Investigation Requested into Juror in Lindsay Clancy Case
related_stories.summary: Lindsay Clancy's attorney has filed a motion requesting the court to investigate a juror who was a holdout during her murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. The motion seeks to examine the juror's cellphone use during deliberations and assess the accuracy of his responses on pre-trial questionnaires and during questioning by the judge.

related_stories.title: FIFA President Proposes Review of Governance Amid Investment Controversy
related_stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called for a consultation to review the decision-making processes of the organization. This proposal follows significant backlash regarding a failed plan to introduce private investment into the World Cup. The German Football Association has criticized Infantino's initiative, suggesting it may be a tactic for his re-election.
